assertions.description: The WebTransport constructor the feature extends is exposed.
WebTransport.prototype exposes the responseHeaders attribute (the feature's only honestly detectable half; requires the WebTransportHeaders flag in Chrome 153).

Constructing with a headers option never throws regardless of support (unknown dictionary members are silently dropped) — which is exactly why construction success must not be used as a support probe. Holds on every engine with WebTransport.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://unreachable.invalid:4433/', { headers: { 'x-conf': '1' } }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); t.close(); return true; } catch (e) { return false; } })()

assertions.description: responseHeaders reads null between construction and session establishment.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !('responseHeaders' in WebTransport.prototype)) return false; const t = new WebTransport('https://unreachable.invalid:4433/'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const early = t.responseHeaders; t.close(); return early === null; })()

assertions.description: Headers passed via WebTransportOptions are carried on the extended CONNECT and observable server-side; responseHeaders exposes the server's reply headers after ready.
assertions.test: Requires a reachable HTTP/3 WebTransport endpoint that echoes or logs CONNECT headers: connect via the handshake-lab demo with an authorization header and verify the server received it and that responseHeaders lists the server's reply entries.
